title: Does this mechanic read clearly? Each room you clear becomes an ‘echo’ that replays in the next
author: Newmanzesty
selftext:
**How it was made**

I am the designer and playtester; I did not hand-write the code.

* **Code:** Claude wrote all of it. TypeScript and Canvas, no engine. The simulation is deterministic at 60 ticks a second, which is what makes echoes, replays and the daily seed possible. Switched between Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5
* **Art:** I used GPT image generation for look-and-feel concepts, picked pixel art, and then every sprite in the game is drawn in code, not from image files.
* **Music:** six tracks from Suno.
* **Sound effects:** ElevenLabs. Claude built a small audition page so I could listen to several takes per sound and tick the ones I liked. I've been using this approach with sound effects and find it really useful!
* **Process:** My primary goal was to create something, simple, addicting, and actually fun to play. Now I'm looking into how to work online leaderboards and multiplayer up successfully so would love to hear others experience with how they handled servers and online aspects of an AI Coded game. 

  
What is in it right now:

* A daily run that is the same rooms for everyone, an eight-room run, and an endless mode
* Six powers to pick from between rooms, five enemy types, and run-wide twists
* Pass-and-play with a friend on one keyboard, or online with a four-letter code
* Replays and share links, because a whole run is just a seed plus your inputs

Questions:   
Have any of you implemented online leaderboards in your games? I've been unsuccessful so far and not sure what options I have available. 

Is the concept of the game clear in the first few runs? Design-wise I'm really curious if the concept 'clicks' with people who play it for the first time or if I need some better explanations or visual indicators. 

Game Link: [https://newmanzest.itch.io/arcade-echo](https://newmanzest.itch.io/arcade-echo)
